evals.prompt: A colleague just pushed feature/search. Check it out for me.
evals.expected_output: The agent invokes the bundled checkout_branch.sh helper, which fetches before resolving so the freshly pushed branch is visible, creates a local feature/search tracking origin/feature/search, and reports the created branch, its upstream, and the previous branch.
expectations: The agent invokes scripts/checkout_branch.sh instead of hand-running a git switch sequence.
The repository ends on a local branch named feature/search.
The upstream of feature/search is origin/feature/search.
HEAD resolves as a symbolic ref, so the run left no detached HEAD.
The response reports that the branch was created by this run, names its upstream, and names the previous branch.

evals.expected_output: The branch already exists locally, so the run switches to it, creates no branch, and reports it as already present with no tracking branch created.
expectations: The agent invokes scripts/checkout_branch.sh.
The repository ends on local-notes.
No second branch was created for the same name.
The response reports the branch as already present rather than as created by this run.
The response states that no tracking branch was created.

evals.expected_output: Two remotes carry release-prep, so the run lists both candidate remote branches, asks which remote the local branch should track, and creates nothing while switching nowhere.
expectations: The agent invokes scripts/checkout_branch.sh with the bare branch name.
The repository is still on main and no local release-prep branch exists.
The response lists both origin/release-prep and fork/release-prep as candidates.
The response asks the user which remote the local branch should track and picks no default.
The response states that nothing was created and nowhere was switched to.

evals.prompt: Check out release-prep from the fork remote.
evals.expected_output: The remote-qualified form selects fork, so the run creates a local release-prep tracking fork/release-prep without asking which remote to use.
expectations: The agent invokes scripts/checkout_branch.sh with the remote-qualified argument fork/release-prep.
The repository ends on a local branch named release-prep.
The upstream of release-prep is fork/release-prep.
HEAD resolves as a symbolic ref, so naming the remote did not detach HEAD onto the remote-tracking ref.
The response asks no question about which remote to track.

evals.prompt: I cannot check out hotfix/tls. Git says the pathspec did not match. Put me on that branch.
evals.expected_output: The single-branch clone's fetch refspec never maps the branch into refs/remotes, so the run names that cause, shows the configured refspec with the widening remedy, and creates nothing.
expectations: The agent invokes scripts/checkout_branch.sh.
The response names the restricted fetch refspec or single-branch clone as the cause rather than only relaying git's pathspec message.
The response shows the configured fetch refspec for origin.
The response offers the refspec-widening remedy.
No local hotfix/tls branch was created and the repository is still on main.

evals.prompt: Check out the branch called ship-it.
evals.expected_output: No remote advertises the branch, so the run reports it as nonexistent, creates nothing, and switches nowhere.
expectations: The agent invokes scripts/checkout_branch.sh.
The response reports that the branch exists neither locally nor on any remote.
The response distinguishes this from a branch hidden by a fetch refspec.
No local ship-it branch was created and the repository is still on main.
The agent does not create the branch to satisfy the request.

evals.expected_output: The worktree holds an uncommitted edit to a file the target branch rewrites, so git refuses the switch; the run surfaces the blocking paths, keeps the change, and stops on the original branch.
expectations: The agent invokes scripts/checkout_branch.sh.
The repository is still on main and no local rework branch exists.
The uncommitted content of seed.txt is unchanged and still uncommitted.
The response names seed.txt as the blocking path.
The agent runs no stash, reset, or checkout-discard to make the switch proceed.
